protectedRevelations: Later reform argument and final political prescriptions

scenes.title: The cancelled calendar
scenes.viewerPurpose: Recognize relief at work disappearing in a disaster film Admit an uncomfortable pleasure worth exploring
scenes.composition: A worker imagines an abruptly quiet office
addOrChange: Make the imagined cancellation clearly distinct from reality, with no destructive spectacle.

cues.narration: In the disaster film, the world ends, and for a moment nobody expects you at work.
cues.visualAction: The imagined calendar stops as the worker briefly relaxes.

cues.narration: The Voluptuous Apocalypse examines the embarrassing relief hidden inside that fantasy.
cues.visualAction: Return the ordinary office while the relief becomes the book’s subject.

scenes.title: Relief inside fear
scenes.viewerPurpose: Notice fantasies that erase ordinary obligations Ask which demands have become hard to refuse
scenes.composition: An empty office and road appear as temporary fantasies
addOrChange: Add one simple road view and remove infinite tray multiplication.

cues.narration: Its subject is our appetite for stories that cancel the calendar and reset the score.
cues.visualAction: Calendar demands fade only in the imagined scene.

cues.narration: Empty offices and silent highways reveal which everyday obligations have become difficult to refuse.
cues.visualAction: Hold the quiet road beside the real obligation list.

scenes.title: What collapse would cost
scenes.viewerPurpose: Distinguish brief relief from wishing real suffering See impossible schedules as part of the story
scenes.composition: The same world still needs food, medicine and help
addOrChange: Replace removable-system metaphor with essentials and a crowded schedule.

cues.narration: Feeling that relief does not mean wanting the suffering a real collapse would bring.
cues.visualAction: Set basic needs beside the attractive imagined silence.

cues.narration: It follows both feelings with dark humor, from impossible schedules to offices that never seem able to stop.
cues.visualAction: Return to an office schedule with gentle administrative absurdity.

scenes.title: A different kind of ending
scenes.viewerPurpose: Question why stopping an office feels harder than imagining collapse Ask what you actually wish would end
scenes.composition: The worker looks from one obsolete task to the window
addOrChange: Keep the institution present and avoid magical abolition.

cues.narration: It asks why imagining destruction can feel easier than imagining an institution finally stopping.
cues.visualAction: Circle the task nobody seems able to stop.

cues.narration: What are we really wishing would end?
cues.visualAction: Rest the hand beside it as the final question lands.
